## Private-repository workflow

Every assignment is distributed through a private GitHub repository created
for you. Accept the GitHub invitation, clone the repository through RStudio,
and work inside that RStudio Project. Your ordinary cycle is:

1. edit and save source files;
2. run code and render the Quarto document;
3. inspect the Git diff;
4. commit a coherent change;
5. push to GitHub; and
6. inspect the latest GitHub Actions run.

The latest commit pushed before the deadline is the submitted version. A green
automated check verifies specified mechanical and computational requirements;
it does not evaluate the quality of an explanation or substantive argument.

See [GitHub and RStudio](setup/github-rstudio.qmd) for the complete first-time
workflow.

## A4: simulation and sampling distributions

**Due October 14 at 1:30 p.m. Pacific.** A4 develops PSD Exercises **5.14,
5.30, 5.31, and 5.38** with guided simulations, density plots, and comparisons
of cumulative probabilities. See the
[Seminar 6 materials](meetings/06-sampling-distributions/index.qmd), especially
Demo 8b for the probability comparisons and Demo 11 for the t statistic.

Accept the invitation to your private A4 repository and clone it as a new
RStudio project. Complete `R/a4_answers.R` and the written responses in the
QMD. Save, run the visible checks, and render the report. Commit and push
**the answers R file, QMD, and current HTML**. The supplied helpers produce
the plots and tables; automated checks provide feedback rather than a grade.

## B2: random variables and decisions

**Due October 7 at 1:30 p.m. Pacific.** B2 uses bargaining data to study
discrete random variables, transformed earnings, and decisions under uncertainty.
A hypothetical election forecast connects a continuous normal margin to a
discrete contract payoff. See the
[Seminar 5 materials](meetings/05-continuous-random-variables/index.qmd)
for worked examples and the R demonstration.

Accept the invitation to your private B2 repository and clone it as a new
RStudio project. The data and plotting helpers are included. Follow the
repository's README for the local checks, and commit both your completed
QMD and freshly rendered HTML. Automated checks do not grade your reasoning.

## A2: calculation and simulation

**Due September 16 at 1:30 p.m.** A2 uses PSD exercises **2.1, 2.3, 2.4, 2.7,
2.9, 2.33, and 2.36**, covering §§2.1, 2.2, and 2.4. Exercises 2.7, 2.9, and
2.36 ask you to compare analytical and simulated answers. Follow the detailed
instructions in your private repository, including the named R objects and
visible checks. See the [Seminar 2 materials](meetings/02-probability/index.qmd)
for worked examples of the workflow.

## Getting your repository

GitHub sends an invitation to the account whose username you provided to the
instructor. Check both your email and [GitHub notifications](https://github.com/notifications).
After accepting, the repository appears under the `POLI210-2026` organization.
Do not make it public, transfer it, or add other collaborators.

If an invitation or repository is missing, email the instructor with your
GitHub username. Do not send a password or authentication token.
